budgetStatus.note: The frozen 250ms budget is exceeded by the current implementation. This is the P4R-0 finding, not a P4R-0 failure: P4R-1 owns the fix. The budget must not be raised to accommodate it.
budgetStatus.loadSensitivityCause: Process-spawn cost swings roughly 12x with invocation context (measured ~9-11ms direct, ~117-122ms under npm), and detectGitRuntime() is uncached so every git-touching route pays it per call. An earlier revision of this file blamed PATH length; that explanation was tested and DISPROVED, and the real cause is not established. Compare readings only within the same calibration — see baselineObservation.calibration.
budgetStatus.structuralFinding: interaction is one-time dominated (its cost disappears on a second call); changesets and workspace-status are recurring costs paid by every view. P4R-1 should target the recurring pair, not the one-time creation.
budgetStatus.violationAttribution: The recorded peak is the one-time interaction ChangeSet creation, which is OUT of P4R-1 scope. The routes P4R-1 owns are under budget at this revisionCount and exceed it as revisions accumulate. P4R-1 is accountable for the recurring pair and for the growth term, not for this peak.

checks.detail: Baseline corpus was produced by real run_tool -> tool_job -> artifact truth runs, not a database seed.
Every route the baseline must measure returned 200, so the timings are the real path and not argument validation.
Event-loop delay came from a real histogram sample, not the empty-histogram sentinel.
The authoritative >250ms signal is declared as the 10ms-resolution histogram; the 1Hz tick sampler is explicitly rejected as unable to resolve it.
Metrics with no producer are recorded as unmeasured with a stated reason, never estimated or defaulted to zero.
Every writable path is redirected and guarded from one declared list, so a capture cannot reach the developer database or the real user data root.
The probe is env-gated: with the flag unset every export is a no-op and the /api/__perf surface is not mounted.
The corpus creates and owns a real project, without which every Result Studio route rejects and the baseline would time validation.
Every measured route records both a first-call and a second-call timing, so one-time creation cost cannot be reported as steady-state viewing cost.

The four plan invariants exist as tests written against code reality, each naming the concrete defect it fails on. They are deliberately NOT aggregated into this gate: three fail today, which is P4R-0 delivering a definition of done for P4R-1 and P4R-5, not a passing claim.
All declared P4R-0 command gates passed.
No recorded gate invokes bare `npm test`, which under a file filter resolves to `vitest run --changed`, selects nothing and reports success for a zero-test run.
